judgments.reasoning_cat1: It conditions the whole sale on 'the conditions set forth in Section 11 hereof', but Section 11 contains no conditions, and it refers to 'the Swap Agreements', a term never defined in this Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the Cut-off Date Balance definition ($735,100,463.83) and Section 14, it makes each of two sellers deliver a pool equal to the whole pool balance and points to the wrong conditions section, an inconsistency Section 20 repeats.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite closing-mechanics sentence with an express fallback to agreement of the parties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Closing Date definition and Section 14; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Again keys payment to 'the conditions set forth in Section 11 hereof', which are not there, and the Acquisition Price it directs be paid is blank in Section 1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The conditions to the Purchaser's obligations are in Section 14(a), and Section 20 compounds the error by calling them Section 11(a) and (b); the mis-citation runs through the payment obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It re-defines 'the Mortgage Loan Schedule' and requires provision 'as of the date hereof' while also requiring delivery 'on the Closing Date', a small internal wobble.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 already defines Mortgage Loan Schedule with a 33-item list and states it is attached as Exhibit 2, whereas this section says the Schedule sets out the different information listed on Exhibit 2 and is still to be agreed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The phrase 'and all payments thereof' is appended to both sides of the allocation without explaining what it adds, leaving prepayments and recoveries after the Cut-off Date unallocated on the face of the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The attached Underlying Agreement allocates interest from the Closing Date rather than the Cut-off Date, and Section 6(b) cross-refers to 'Section 4' for what the Purchaser would own, so the allocation matters elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence of enormous length with three lettered substitutes and two further provisos; clause (z) refers to notes 'each identified in the list delivered by the Purchaser to the Trustee ... and attached hereto as Exhibit 6', which is confusing as to who identifies lost notes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit 6 is a blank 'Available Upon Request' page and the 180-day recording duty is qualified by Section 6(a), which is itself garbled and refers to a non-existent Section 5(c) and (d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It obliges 'EMC or MSMCH, as applicable' to act 'at EMC's own expense', so MSMCH's performance is expressly funded by EMC, an apparent slip that changes who pays.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also purports to bind the Master Servicer ('the Master Servicer agrees that it will not'), a party to the Pooling and Servicing Agreement but not a signatory here, and ties the covenant to the PSA's term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear preservation of remedies notwithstanding examination; 'such due diligence as any such party reasonably believes is appropriate' is a mild open standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 19 describes 'the cure, purchase or substitution obligations contained in Sections 5 and 7 hereof', but Section 5 contains no such obligations, which puts this section at odds with the assignment provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanics of substitution and release are set out concretely, though 'the selected Mortgage Loan' is an undefined phrase in context.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imposes obligations on the Trustee, a non-party, and Section 19 wrongly identifies this Section 5 as the home of the sellers' cure/purchase/substitution obligations, which actually sit in Section 10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is plainly corrupt: it breaks off at 'at no expense to' and resumes mid-list, the enumeration uses '(iv)' twice, and there is no '(i)'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It declares a failure to record a 'Material Defect' and says 'the provisions of Section 5(c) and (d) shall apply', but Section 5 has only subsections (a) and (b), and 'Material Defect' is defined nowhere in this Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional true-sale/backup-security-interest clause; the citation to UCC 'Section 9-305' for possession is out of date under revised Article 9 but the intent is legible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Section 4 for the Purchaser's entitlements and to accounts under the Pooling and Servicing Agreement, and sits consistently with Section 6(b)'s counterpart in the Underlying Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as to itself in the capacity indicated' is an unexplained qualifier, since no capacities are separately indicated in Section 7.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs the reps to MSMCH as well as the Purchaser, which is unusual given Section 19 assigns the Purchaser's rights to the Trustee; no direct conflict though.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate organization and good-standing rep with a materiality carve-out; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 9(a) for MSMCH and Section 28's continuing existence covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Sections 9(b) and 13(b); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard authorization/no-conflict rep; 'hereof or thereof' refers to a 'thereof' with no antecedent, a harmless carryover.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Sections 9(c) and 13(c); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-consent rep with an express carve-out for pending recordations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recordation carve-out lines up with Sections 4(b) and 6(a); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard enforceability rep with the usual bankruptcy qualification.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'and EMC not in default with respect to any order' omits the verb 'is', a mechanical error, and 'in the judgment of EMC' makes the second limb subjective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel MSMCH rep in Section 9(f) contains the missing word, highlighting the slip but creating no substantive conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It relies on a term, 'the Mortgage Loan Seller's Information', that it says is defined elsewhere and gives no content to here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14(a), the cited source, contains no definition of Mortgage Loan Seller's Information anywhere in its four numbered conditions, so the disclosure rep has no defined subject matter.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'has full right and authority to subject to no interest or participation of' is grammatically broken, and the section heading promises warranties 'concerning the EMC Mortgage Loans' while only an ownership warranty follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Unlike Section 10, this section provides no cure/repurchase/substitution remedy for EMC, yet Section 19 speaks of 'the cure, purchase or substitution obligations' of 'the Mortgage Loan Sellers', leaving the EMC loans' remedy structure unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as to itself in the capacity indicated' is the same unexplained qualifier as in Section 7 but is otherwise plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 7's structure; no conflicting provision identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate organization and good-standing rep; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 7(a) and Section 28's covenant as to MSMCH's LLC existence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line corporate power rep; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Sections 7(b) and 13(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-conflict rep; the reference to conflicting with 'the written consent of the sole member or formation agreement' is awkward but comprehensible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14(a)(2)(iii) requires delivery of that written consent and operating agreement, so the pieces fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-consent rep with a recordation carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Section 7(d) and consistent with Sections 4(b) and 6(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading says 'Concerning the Mortgage Loans' without limiting to MSMCH's own loans, and 'as of the Closing Date or such other date as may be specified below' leaves the speaking date open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (a) then covers 'each Mortgage Loan' (including EMC's) while subsection (b) covers only MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans, and Section 8 gives EMC a separate, narrower warranty, so the scope of MSMCH's undertaking is genuinely contestable.
